sections.title: Article heading
sections.text:
ARTICLE 1094.

PD 1094.

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1094.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 1094 was established by Ordinance No. 32337, passed by the Dallas City Council on October 26, 2022. (Ord. 32337)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1094.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 1094 is established on property located at the northeast line of Orinda Drive west of Preston Road. The size of PD 1094 is approximately 6.802 acres. (Ord. 32337)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1094.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article. In this article:

(1) ELECTRIC VEHICLE SUPPLY EQUIPMENT (EVSE) means the conductors, including the ungrounded, grounded, and equipment grounding conductors, and the electric vehicle connectors, attachment plugs, and all other fittings, devices, power outlets, or apparatus installed specifically for the purpose of transferring energy between the premises wiring and the electric vehicle.

(2) EV CAPABLE means electric capacity, conduit, and space to support a circuit for each EV parking space, and the installation of raceways, both underground and surface mounted, as required, to support the EVSE.

(3) EV INSTALLED means a designated parking space with a branch circuit for EVSE servicing electric vehicles and an electric vehicle charging station installed.

(4) EV READY means a designated parking space which is provided with one dedicated branch circuit for EVSE servicing electric vehicles.

(5) INTERNAL DRIVEWAY means a vehicular drive for means of ingress and egress to the site accessed from Preston Road or Orinda Drive. Fire lanes for emergency access only are not included in this definition.

(6) MICRO-MOBILITY CHARGING means an electrical charging station or outlet available for charging micro-mobility vehicles such as e-scooters and e-bikes.

(7) NEW CONSTRUCTION means construction of a main structure that did not exist as of October 26, 2022.

(8) PARKWAY means that portion of a street or highway between the curb lines or the lateral lines of a roadway and the adjacent sidewalk, not intended for the use of pedestrians.

(9) STREET-FRONTING FACADE means the building face fronting Preston Road or Orinda Drive.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district. (Ord. 32337)

sections.title: Exhibit
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1094.104. EXHIBIT.

The following exhibit is incorporated into this article: Exhibit 1094A: conceptual plan. (Ord. 32337)

sections.title: Vision Statement
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1094.105. VISION STATEMENT.

This district is envisioned to be a vibrant mixed-use, mixed-income development with pedestrian-friendly elements and open space strategically dispersed throughout the site resulting in pedestrian connectivity both internally to the site and externally to the surrounding area. The existing adjacent residential areas will be protected by height restrictions resulting from the residential proximity slope and additional landscaping buffers developed on the Property. This development is intended to provide a desirable live, work, play environment which will enhance the vitality of the surrounding area for the future. (Ord. 32337)

sections.title: Conceptual Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1094.106. CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the conceptual plan (Exhibit 1094A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the conceptual plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 32337)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1094.107. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) For work other than repair of existing structures, demolition and grading, installation of fencing or other structures for security purposes, work associated with permitted temporary uses, or work intended to provide for the irrigation or maintenance of landscaping, a

development plan must be approved by the city plan commission before the issuance of any building permit to authorize work in this district.

(b) A development plan is not required to include all phases of development if separate phases are proposed. If separate phases are proposed, a development plan for each phase must be approved by the city plan commission before the issuance of a building permit to authorize work in that phase of development.

(c) If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the development plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 32337)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1094.108. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Except as provided in this section, the only main uses permitted are those main uses permitted in the MU-2 Mixed Use District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the MU-2 Mixed Use District, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the MU-2 Mixed Use District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this district only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the MU-2 Mixed Use District is subject to DIR in this district; etc.

(b) The following main uses are prohibited:

(1) Commercial and business service uses.

-- Labor hall. -- Tool or equipment rental.

(2) Industrial uses.

-- Gas drilling and production. -- Temporary concrete or asphalt batching plant.

(3) Institutional and community service uses.

-- Cemetery or mausoleum. -- Halfway house. -- Hospital.

(4) Lodging uses.

-- Extended stay hotel or motel. -- Hotel or motel. -- Overnight general purpose shelter.

(5) Miscellaneous uses.

-- Carnival or circus (temporary).

(6) Office uses.

-- Alternative financial establishment. -- Financial institution with drive-in window.

(7) Retail and personal service uses.

-- Animal shelter or clinic without outside runs. -- Auto service center. -- Car wash. -- Commercial amusement (inside). -- Commercial amusement (outside). -- Convenience store with drive-through. -- General merchandise or food store 100,000 square feet or more. -- Mortuary, funeral home, or commercial wedding chapel. -- Motor vehicle fueling station. -- Restaurant with drive-in or drive-through service. -- Theater. (Ord. 32337)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1094.109. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217. (Ord. 32337)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1094.110. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. If there is a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the MU-2 Mixed Use District apply.

(b) Front yard. Minimum front yard is 50 feet on Preston Road as shown on the conceptual plan.

(c) Side and rear yard.

(1) Northern property line and adjacent MF-1(A) multifamily district. Minimum side and rear yard are 50 feet from the northern Property line and adjacent MF-1(A) zoning districts as shown on the conceptual plan.

(2) Orinda Drive. Minimum side and rear yard are 15 feet from Orinda Drive as shown on the conceptual plan.

(d) Density.

(1) In general.

(i) Minimum number of dwelling units is 250.

(ii) Except as provided in this subsection, maximum dwelling unit density is 50 dwelling units per acre.

(2) Increased development standards.

(i) If compliant with Section 51P-1094.118(a)(1), maximum dwelling unit density is 85 dwelling units per acre.

(ii) If compliant with Section 51P-1094.118(a)(2), maximum dwelling unit density is 105 dwelling units per acre.

(e) Floor area ration and floor area.

(1) Non-residential uses. Non-residential uses may not exceed 30 percent of the total floor area per building site.

(2) Increased development standards for residential uses. If compliant with Section 51P-1094.118(a)(1) or Section 51P-1094.118(a)(2), no maximum floor area ratio for residential uses.

(3) Mix of uses. Retail and personal service uses are limited to a maximum of 30,000 square feet of floor area and must be located in a mixed-use project.

(f) Stories. No maximum number of stories.

(g) Encroachments. The following additional items are permitted to be located within the required front, side, and rear yards:

(1) Seat walls, retaining walls, stoops, porches, steps, unenclosed balconies, ramps, handrails, safety railings, and benches all not exceeding four feet in height and extending a maximum of five feet into the required minimum yards.

(2) Landscape planters.

(3) Sculptures.

(4) Awnings

(h) Compliance. For purposes of compliance with yard, lot, and space regulations, the Property is considered one lot. (Ord. 32337)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1094.111. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, consult the use regulations in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(1) Multifamily parking. If compliant with Sections 51P-1094.118(a)(1) or 51P-1094.118(a)(2), a minimum of one-half space per dwelling unit is required, or per the requirements of Division 51A-4.200, whichever requires fewer spaces.

(2) Retirement housing. One-quarter space per dwelling unit is required, or per the requirements of Division 51A-4.200, whichever requires fewer spaces.

(3) Affordable units. Required off-street parking for the affordable units must be available as free parking.

(b) Parking structure. A minimum of 80 percent of provided parking must be located in a parking structure.

(c) Aboveground parking structures. Aboveground parking structures must be screened or wrapped in accordance with this subsection. If an aboveground parking structure is facing Preston Road, Orinda Drive, or an internal driveway as shown on the conceptual plan, the aboveground parking structure must be wrapped in accordance with this subsection.

(1) Screening of parking structures. Except for openings for vehicular access, openings in aboveground parking structure facades must provide solid screening with a painted, stained, or masonry-like finish a minimum of 42 inches from the floor level within the parking structure to screen vehicles and vehicle headlights.

(2) Wrapping of parking structures. Except for openings for vehicular access, aboveground parking structures must be wrapped with a use other than parking, to a minimum depth of 25 feet of the building measured inward from the exterior facing structure facade.

(d) Surface parking location. Surface parking is prohibited between the public or private street-facing facade and the property line. For the purposes of this subsection, surface parking means at grade parking not within or under a structure.

(e) Bike parking. Bike parking for at least 10 percent of the dwelling units must be provided in the parking garages, in a secure location near the building entrance.

(f) Electrical vehicle charging. A minimum of 10 percent of provided parking must be equipped with electric vehicle charging stations, with the required type of spaces as follows:

(1) A minimum of two percent of provided off-street parking spaces must be EV installed parking spaces;

(2) A minimum of two percent of provided off-street parking spaces must be EV ready; and

(3) A minimum of six percent of provided off-street parking spaces must be EV capable.

(g) EV ready parking spaces. EV ready parking space must include a circuit that terminates in a suitable termination point such as a receptacle or junction box and be located in close proximity to the proposed location of the EV parking spaces.

(h) Micro-mobility charging stations. Charging stations for at least 10 micro-mobility vehicles must be provided and must be located outside of the right-of-way and sidewalks. The charging stations must be designed to allow the possibility to secure the vehicles.

(i) Assigned parking. For assigned parking spaces, those spaces allotted for reserved dwelling units must be dispersed and distributed amongst all other assigned parking for similar units.

(j) Passenger loading and residential deliveries.

(1) Each building site must provide at least two off-street or on-street passenger loading and residential delivery spaces. The board of adjustment may grant a variance to this subparagraph.

(2) On-street passenger loading zones, if provided, must be constructed in compliance with Architectural Barrier Act accessibility standards and must be approved by the director and by the director of public works.

(k) Service, loading, and garbage storage areas. Except for passenger loading and residential deliveries, service, loading, and garbage storage areas must be enclosed within a main structure. (Ord. 32337)

sections.title: Ingress-Egress
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1094.112. INGRESS-EGRESS

Two points of ingress and egress must be provided for each submitted development plan as shown as approximate point of access on the conceptual plan. (Ord. 32337)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1094.113. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 32337)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1094.114. LANDSCAPING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(b) Landscape plan. A landscape plan must be submitted with a development plan and approved by the city plan commission before issuance of building permit to authorize work in this district. The landscape plan must include the full phase of the submitted development plan.

(c) Protected tree mitigation. Replacement trees must have a caliper of at least three inches.

(d) Perimeter landscape buffer.

(1) A 15-foot enhanced landscape buffer is required along Orinda Drive and internal driveways as shown on the conceptual plan.

(2) A 50-foot enhanced landscape buffer is required along Preston Road as shown on the conceptual plan.

(3) Sidewalks and pedestrian facilities may be located within the required perimeter landscape buffer.

(e) Street trees. A minimum of one large canopy tree with a minimum caliper of six- inches or greater is required for every 30 feet of street frontage along Preston Road, Orinda Drive, and internal driveways as shown on the conceptual plan and within the perimeter landscape buffer as required by subsection (d). Existing healthy trees with an eight-inch caliper or greater located within the perimeter landscape buffer must be preserved and may count toward the street tree requirement.

(f) Parking lot trees. All parking spaces in a surface lot may not be more than 60 feet from a large canopy tree planted in a median or an island. Each parking lot tree must have a minimum caliper of three-inches and may not be planted closer than three feet to a paved portion of the parking lot. A median or island in a surface parking lot must be a minimum of 125 square feet in area.

(g) Parkway. Parkway must be of a pervious surface and planted. Street trees or landscaping must be located in the parkway.

(h) Plants. Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 32337)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1094.115. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts in Article VII. (Ord. 32337)

sections.title: Open Space
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1094.116. OPEN SPACE

(a) Unrestricted open space. A minimum of 20 percent of each building site must be reserved as unrestricted open space for activity such as active or passive recreation, community gathering space, or landscaping, and must be located between the exterior structure facade and the property line.

(b) Linear open space along Preston Road. An unrestricted linear open space with a minimum width of 50 feet must be provided along Preston Road as shown on the conceptual plan.

(c) Interior open space. Of the required 20 percent open space, a minimum 10 percent is required to be interior open space provided along internal driveways, perimeter landscape buffers along Orinda Drive as shown on the conceptual plan, and any other open space areas excluding the minimum 50-foot linear open space along Preston Road as shown on the conceptual plan.

(d) Contiguous open space. Of the required 20 percent open space, a minimum of 70 percent must be contiguous open space in the form of a park, plaza, pedestrian area, or central green space.

(e) Open space requirements. All open space must comply with the following provisions.

(1) No structures except for architectural elements; playground equipment; structures that are not fully enclosed such as pergolas and gazebos and ordinary projections of windowsills, bay windows, belt courses, cornices, eaves, and other architectural features are allowed; otherwise, open space must be open to the sky.

(2) Open space must contain primarily grass, vegetation, or pedestrian areas; and must contain the pedestrian amenities required by Subsection (f).

(3) Parking spaces, drive aisles, and areas primarily intended for vehicular use are not considered open space and do not count towards the open space requirement.

(4) Except for emergency and grounds maintenance vehicles, operation or parking of vehicles within open space is prohibited.

(5) Landscape areas that fulfill the requirements of Article X may also fulfill these requirements if all conditions of this section and Article X are met.

(6) Open space must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance, and plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition.

(f) Pedestrian amenities. Within required open space, a minimum of eight of the following pedestrian amenities are required per building site:

(1) Bike racks.

(2) Bioswale/low impact water retention.

(3) Dog park.

(4) Drinking fountains.

(5) Low-water, native plantings.

(6) Micro-mobility charging stations.

(7) Pedestrian plaza.

(8) Pedestrian-scaled lighting fixture.

(9) Pedestrian-scaled shade structures.

(10) Pet waste stations.

(11) Picnic table.

(12) Playground equipment.

(13) Public art.

(14) Shaded seating areas.

(15) Water features. (Ord. 32337)

sections.title: Sidewalks
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1094.117. SIDEWALKS.

(a) Except as provided in this section, a minimum six-foot-wide unobstructed sidewalk must be provided along Orinda Drive and internal driveways to ensure pedestrian connectivity and not interfere with the preservation of existing, healthy trees.

(b) A minimum eight-foot-wide unobstructed sidewalk and a minimum eight-foot- wide parkway must be provided along Preston Road.

(c) Enhanced pavement must be provided at vehicular drop-offs and motor courts.

(d) Along Preston Road and Orinda Drive, at least one bench and one trash receptacle must be provided for every 300 linear feet of street frontage.

(e) Tree grates do not count toward the minimum unobstructed sidewalk width. (Ord. 32337)

sections.title: Development Bonus For Mixed Income Housing
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1094.118. DEVELOPMENT BONUS FOR MIXED INCOME HOUSING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, compliance with Division 51A- 4.1100, as amended, is required to obtain the development bonuses in Section 51P-1094.110(d)(2) and Section 51P-1094.110(e)(2).

(1) The density and floor area ratio development bonuses set forth in Section 51P-1094.110(d)(2)(i) and Section 51P-1094.110(e)(2) apply if a minimum of five percent of the total number of units are available to households earning between 61 and 80 percent of area median family income.

(2) The density and floor area ratio development bonuses set forth in Section 51P-1094.110(d)(2)(ii) and Section 51P-1094.110(e)(2) apply if a minimum of 10 percent of the total number of units are available to households earning between 61 and 80 percent of area median family income.

(b) Design standards. Compliance with Section 51A-4.1107 is not required. (Ord. 32337)

sections.title: Design Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1094.119. DESIGN STANDARDS.

(a) New construction. The following design standards apply to new construction for all uses.

(1) Street, internal driveway, and open space frontages.

(i) Frontages. All street-fronting facades, internal driveway-fronting facades, and open-space fronting facades must have at least one window and at least one common primary entrance facing the street, internal driveway, or open space at ground level. The entrance must access the street, internal driveway, or open space with an improved path connecting to the sidewalk. A transparent surface is required for every 25 linear feet of continuous street-fronting, internal driveway-fronting, and open-space fronting facade.

(ii) Individual entries. Except as provided in this paragraph, a minimum of 60 percent of the ground level dwelling units adjacent to a street or internal driveway in each building must have individual entries that access the street or internal driveway with an improved path connecting to the sidewalk. For at-grade open space, a minimum of 60 percent of the open- space fronting dwelling units in each building must have individual entries that access the open space. EXCEPTION. This paragraph does not apply to retirement housing.

(2) Lighting.

(i) Special lighting requirement. Exterior lighting sources, if used, must be oriented down and onto the property they light and generally away from adjacent residential properties.

(ii) Pedestrian scale lighting. For a development greater than 20,000 square feet of floor area, pedestrian scale lighting that provides a minimum average illumination level of 1.5 foot candles must be provided along public sidewalks and adjacent public streets and internal driveways. The design and placement of both the standards and fixtures must be approved by the director or transportation.

(3) Non-required fences. Unless a use specifically requires screening, all fences for uses along a street or trail must have a surface area that is a minimum of 50 percent open, allowing visibility between three feet and six feet above grade. This provision does not apply to the south Property line. The exceptions for multifamily districts in Section 51A-4.602(a)(2) and 51A-4.602(a)(4) which provide that a fence exceeding four feet above grade may be erected in a front yard in multifamily districts are not applicable. (Ord. 32337)

sections.title: Transit   Ridership                      Incentives             And
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1094.120 TRANSIT RIDERSHIP INCENTIVES AND ENHANCEMENTS.

(a) This district is intended to enhance public transportation ridership options by providing the following incentives and enhancements detailed in this section.

(b) In order to obtain a development bonus under Section 51P-1094.110, the developer or operator must partner with Dallas Area Rapid Transit for a residential pass program or similar incentive program for at least 30 percent of the dwelling units to ensure transit ridership opportunities for the residents. (Ord. 32337)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1094.121. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 32337)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1094.122. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 32337)
